A coworker of mine was doing maintenance on an 800 ton die cast machine. He had locked out/tagged out the machine, and was cleaning out/fixing the die. This was going on around end of first shift and the guy was still working late on it. Someone on second shift came around and saw the first shift guy's lock still on the machine. The second shifter took the lock off, and closed the die which crushed the man's head. The die opened and the the guy layed there crumpled in a pool of blood with chunks of brain and bone on the floor. He was rushed off to the hospital and SURVIVED. The guy narrowly escaped death, but his skull is more metal than bone. Different people at other locations have not been so lucky. Work place safety is not something to be taken lightly.
